# Enclosed background region recoloring

## When to Use
Use when demos show background-colored cells enclosed by other-color lines being recolored, while exterior background is preserved.

## Procedure
1. Infer boundary, background, and replacement colors from the current demos; palette IDs vary by task.
2. Treat the candidate boundary color as a barrier. Orthogonally flood-fill background cells from all grid edges. Any background cell not reached is topologically enclosed.
3. Replay this classification against every full demo delta. Confirm which enclosed cells change, whether every cavity is targeted, and that exterior/background cells and boundary cells are preserved. Do not assume topological flood-fill if demonstrations imply geometric shape criteria or selective cavity choice.
4. Check diagonal contacts carefully: under 4-neighbor connectivity, diagonal gaps do not seal a region.
5. Apply the evidenced recoloring only; mechanically validate dimensions, row widths, values, and JSON.

## Validated instance example
Continual-ARC task-20212bdc confirms the general rule: recolor every background-colored region enclosed by the line color, including small isolated cells and larger cavities, while leaving the boundary and exterior unchanged. In its demo, background 2 and boundary 0; enclosed cells became 4, including one single-cell cavity and a 4x4 rectangular cavity. The test used background 7 and boundary 9; two enclosed cavities (2x2 and 4x4) were both recolored to 4, while an open/partial shape and the long boundary stripe remained unchanged. This was accepted on the first submission. Re-derive palette roles each task and find all cavities, not just the most salient one.

For this family, enclosed means inaccessible from the outside through orthogonally adjacent background cells when boundary-colored cells are treated as barriers; preserve all other cells. Validate dimensions and every row width mechanically before submitting.

### Distinguish from a selective-frame variant
Some previously observed instances appear selective: only one marked closed shape/cavity is modified despite other linework. Do not assume selectivity without demo evidence. Compare every changed cell and test the all-enclosed-regions hypothesis against the complete demo before choosing.



## Pitfalls
- Enclosures can be irregular; a rectangle-only detector may miss them.
- Do not recolor the boundary, exterior, or all background cells.
- Infer the fill color anew and verify selective behavior across all demonstrations.
